title: Living and not living
keyIdea: Living things eat or drink, grow, and move or change by themselves. People, animals and plants are alive. Rocks, toys and cars are not. Moving is not enough: a toy robot moves, but it cannot eat or grow. Staying still does not mean dead: a tree and a sleeping cat are alive.

kid: A dog is alive. It eats. It drinks. It grows big.
A rock is not alive. It does not eat. It does not grow.
A plant is alive too! It drinks water and it grows.
A toy robot can walk. But it is not alive. It cannot eat. It cannot grow. It stops when the battery runs out.
adult: This topic, for ages 3 to 4, is about sorting things into living (people, animals, plants) and not living (rocks, toys, cars) and giving one simple reason. It is the first step towards the life processes children meet later, such as nutrition, growth, movement and reproduction.

Give your child three easy clues: living things eat or drink, they grow, and they move or change by themselves. A worm eats leaves and wriggles on its own. A seed grows into a plant. A toy car only moves when someone pushes it or a battery runs it, and it never grows.

Common mistakes at this age: thinking anything that moves is alive (cars, clouds, a wind-up toy), thinking plants are not alive because they do not walk, thinking a teddy is alive because it has a face, and thinking a sleeping animal is not alive because it is still. Ask "Does it eat or drink? Does it grow?" rather than "Does it move?"

In the lab your child sorts things into two boxes, watches a seed and a puppy grow while a car and a stone stay the same, feeds a cat, a plant and a teddy, switches on a robot that stops when its battery is flat next to a worm that wriggles by itself, and then sorts the tricky ones.

familyTip: On a walk, play "Alive or not?" Point at a bird, a bench, a tree, a car and a snail. Ask "Does it eat or drink? Does it grow?" before your child decides. Plant a bean in a cup and check it each morning.

practice.hint: Which one eats food and grows bigger?
practice.explain: A bird is alive. It eats, drinks and grows. A spoon and a toy car cannot do any of those.

practice.prompt: Sam plants {n} seeds. He gives them water. Days later, they have grown. Are the seeds alive?
practice.hint: Plants do not walk. What else do living things do?
practice.explain: Yes. Seeds and plants are alive. They drink water and grow, even though they stay in one place.

practice.prompt: A toy robot walks across the floor. Is it alive?
choices: No, a battery makes it go
practice.hint: Can the robot eat? Can it grow?
practice.explain: The robot is not alive. It moves only when a battery runs it, and it can never eat or grow.

practice.prompt: Mia gives food to a puppy and to a teddy. After {n} weeks, which one has grown?
practice.hint: Only one of them can eat the food. Which one?
practice.explain: The puppy has grown. It is alive, so it eats and grows. The teddy cannot eat, and it stays the same size.

practice.prompt: Grandpa's cat is fast asleep on the rug. It does not move. Is it alive?
practice.hint: Does the cat still breathe, eat and grow?
practice.explain: Yes, the cat is alive while it sleeps. Being still does not make something not alive.

pool.hint: Two of these eat or drink and grow. One never does.
pool.explain: A stone is not alive. A tree drinks water and grows, and a fish eats and grows, so they are alive.

pool.prompt: How do we know a flower is alive?
pool.hint: Think of the clues: eat or drink, and grow.
pool.explain: A flower drinks water and grows, so it is alive. Being pretty or smelling nice does not tell you.

pool.prompt: Ben says, "A teddy bear is alive. It has eyes and a mouth." Is he right?
choices: No, a teddy cannot eat or grow
pool.hint: Looks do not tell you. Can the teddy eat?
pool.explain: Ben is not right. A teddy looks like a bear, but it cannot eat, drink or grow, so it is not alive.

pool.prompt: A worm wriggles {n} centimetres to a leaf all by itself and eats it. Is the worm alive?
choices: Yes, it moves by itself and eats
pool.hint: Did anyone push the worm? Did it eat?
pool.explain: The worm is alive. It moves by itself, it eats, and it grows.

pool.prompt: You see a snail, a rock, a bucket and a bush in the garden. Which two are alive?
pool.hint: Which ones eat or drink, and grow?
pool.explain: The snail and the bush are alive. They eat or drink, and grow. A rock and a bucket never grow.

pool.prompt: A toy car rolls {n} steps down a slope. Then it stops. Is the car alive?
choices: No, the slope made it roll
pool.hint: Did the car move by itself, or did the slope do it?
pool.explain: The toy car is not alive. The slope made it roll. It cannot eat, drink or grow.

pool.prompt: What does a living thing need?
pool.hint: What do you give a plant or a pet each day?
pool.explain: Living things need food or water. A battery runs toys, and toys are not alive.

pool.prompt: A tree stands in the park. It never walks anywhere. Is it alive?
choices: No, it is made of wood
pool.hint: Plants do not walk. Do they grow?
pool.explain: The tree is alive. It drinks water through its roots and grows taller each year.

visual.caption: Alive or not alive? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort things into alive and not alive, watch what grows, feed a cat, a plant and a teddy, test a robot and a worm, then sort the tricky ones.
